newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Corruption rises among Russian army officers.
newsitem.headline: Corruption rises among Russian army officers.

text.p: Cases of corruption among Russian army officers have more than doubled this year because of their financial difficulties and poor living conditions, a general said in an interview published on Thursday.

Major-General Yuri Yakovlev, a senior officer in the military prosecutor's office, told the newspaper Komsomolskaya Pravda that 16 generals and more than 80 colonels were under criminal investigation.
The number of officers found guilty of corruption had risen by 109 percent this year, said Yakovlev, whose department oversees all investigations involving the military.
"In the last few years there has been a steady growth in bribe-taking," Yakovlev said.
"The number of officers among those committing the crimes is continually growing."
He said the number of cases of embezzlement in the armed forces had risen by 137 percent this year and that discipline and order had declined.

"A lack of confidence in the future because of cuts in the armed forces...poor living conditions and the lack of social protection for servicemen and their families has led to a deterioration in officers' morale," Yakovlev said.
His comments were the latest sign of problems in the underfunded and demoralised armed forces. Some servicemen have not been paid for months.
Defence Minister Igor Rodionov has been demanding an increase in defence spending and called for extreme measures to save the armed forces from collapse.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Tuesday that military reform would be painful and involve drastic cuts.
